messages:
Maya: Quick product ask: can we add an inline 'Request access' CTA on Route & Model detail pages? Instead of 'Contact admin' that dead-ends people. The flow would create an access request tied to route_id and include suggested role + justification field. Should be light and measurable.

Tomas: +1. Implementation note: don't leak which exact roles exist to callers without view perms. Return a generic suggested_role token like 'route_write' and map client-side to friendly names when allowed.

Priya: We need audit + SLA on requests. Proposed: requests go to a queue, owners get email + Console notification, auto-escalate after 24h. Also add optional one-click approve for org admins.

Maya: Good. UX ask: keep the CTA subtle (text button) and show state: requested / approved / denied. Also show who approved and timestamp.

Tomas: API surface: POST /access-requests {resource_id, scope_hint, justification}. Response: request_id, status. GET /access-requests/{id} for status. Will require caller identity and 2xx only if allowed. We'll rate-limit to 5 reqs/user/min to prevent spam.

Priya: Telemetry: events access_request_created, access_request_viewed_by_admin, access_request_decision. Fields: org_id, resource_type, resource_id, requestor_role_hash, outcome. Important: no PII in events. Use hashed ids.

DesignBot: Microcopy drafts: A) "Request access" CTA + modal header "Request access to this route" B) Success toast: "Request sent — owner notified" C) Denied state: short reason + link to appeals doc. I'll mock variations.

Maya: Edge case: what if the resource has multiple owners? We should send to primary owner + owners_group. Also allow routing to team inbox.

Tomas: On auth side: when a request is auto-approved (policy-based), we should issue a scoped ephemeral grant token (ttl 1h) instead of mutating user roles. That avoids long-lived role churn. Ephemeral grants are logged.

Priya: +1 ephemeral grants. Add event ephemeral_grant_issued with grant_id and ttl. Must include a manual revoke endpoint.

Maya: Can we surface 'simulate access' button for admins to preview effective perms for a user before approving? Helps reduce mistaken grants.

Tomas: We already have an internal simulator API. Expose a limited endpoint: POST /simulate-access {user_hash, resource_id} returning actions_allowed[]. Must be gated to admin roles and should redaction any sensitive results.

DesignBot: For the modal, include a small note: "Owners can approve or request more info. If urgent, mention it in justification." Keep it 1 line.

Priya: Compliance: ensure approval emails do not include justification text for regulated orgs unless allowed. Add an org-level toggle to omit free-text in emails.

Maya: Rollout plan: feature flag 'inline-access-requests' off by default. Canary 5% of orgs + all internal orgs. Measure request volume, approval latency, and support ticket delta.

InfraBot: feature-flag created: inline-access-requests (canary 5% + internal).

Tomas: I'll add the API endpoints and ephemeral-grant plumbing. Plan to return minimal response shapes to keep backwards compatibility.

Priya: I'll create telemetry ticket with schemas and retention rules. Also add an alert for sudden spike in requests (>1000/hr org-level).

Maya: Ok assign: @Tomas API + infra, @DesignBot modal/copy, @Priya telemetry + ops, I'll draft product PR. Follow-up sync Tuesday to review canary metrics.
